newsitem.title: USA: US attache sees continued large China soy imports.
newsitem.headline: US attache sees continued large China soy imports.

text.p: An agricultural attache posted at the U.S. embassy in Beijing forecast China would continue to import large quantities of soybean meal and oil in 1997/98, due to lower domestic production.

The attache forecast China soymeal imports would climb to 2.2 million tonnes in 1997/98 from 2.0 million tonnes seen for 1996/97, The increase would "make up for the shortfall in domestic production and to meet demand spurred by China's rapidly expanding livestock industry."
In a report dated March 3 and released in Washington Tuesday, the attache estimated China soyoil imports at 1.5 million tonnes in 1996/97 and 1.3 million tonnes in 1997/98.
Attache reports are not official USDA data.

The attache forecast calendar year 1996 China soybean production at 13 million tonnes, matching USDA's latest official estimate, and predicted "only a minor recovery" to 13.4 million tonnes in calendar year 1997.

The attache said high grain procurement prices induced many farmers to switch to corn from soybeans. In addition, farmers in the Heilongjiang Province, where over a third of China's soybeans are produced, are still reeling from policies that barred movement of unprocessed soybeans outside the province.
Soybean imports are estimated to double in 1996/97 to 1.6 million tonnes, dropping to 1.5 million tonnes in 1997/98, the attache said.
